core_obligations: Show that f^! exists and reduce to the smooth equidimensional case (proof lines 14488-14497).
Write alpha and beta through caps of bivariant classes and use the value of f^! on the fundamental class (proof lines 14499-14507).

difficulty_reason: For a field k and a proper morphism f : X -> Y of schemes smooth over k, the lemma asserts that the Gysin map exists for f and that f_*(alpha . f^!beta) = f_*alpha . beta (statement lines 14481-14486). The proof shows existence as in the multiplicative case, by exhibiting X -> X x_k Y as an immersion into a scheme smooth over Y and quoting Definition labelled definition-lci-gysin, then reduces to X and Y smooth equidimensional of dimensions d and e by decomposing into connected components (proof lines 14488-14497). Using f^![Y]_e = [X]_d from Lemma labelled lemma-lci-gysin-easy and writing alpha = c cap [X]_d and beta = c' cap [Y]_e by Lemma labelled lemma-identify-chow-for-smooth, the proof runs a seven term chain: pull f^! inside the product, use its value on the fundamental class, swap the two cappings by the commutativity of the intersection product, move the bivariant class c' past f_*, and read the result back as beta . f_*alpha (proof lines 14499-14520). The commutation of f^! with c' is Lemma labelled lemma-lci-gysin-commutes, and the passage of c' through f_* is the definition of a bivariant class. Recognising that the identity reduces to bookkeeping with bivariant classes against a single fundamental class is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
